draft.title: Conservation of mass
card: In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged into new substances. No atoms are made or lost.
Because the atoms stay the same, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.
In an open container, a gas product can escape into the air. The mass left in the container then seems to drop.
In a sealed container, no gas can escape. The total mass stays the same, which shows mass is conserved.
draft.remember: Mass is conserved because atoms are only rearranged, but an escaping gas can hide this.

a.q: Why is the total mass of the products equal to the total mass of the reactants?
opts: Atoms are rearranged, and none are made or lost
Atoms join up, so fewer atoms are left at the end
Atoms change into other atoms with the same mass
Atoms of the reactants are used up completely
a.why: A reaction only rearranges the atoms, so every atom that starts is still there at the end. The idea that atoms are used up is wrong, because they form new substances instead.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the atoms themselves.

b.q: Priya adds an antacid tablet to water in an open cup on a balance. Bubbles of gas form and the reading drops. What is the best explanation?
opts: Gas escaped into the air, taking its mass with it
Some atoms were destroyed when the tablet reacted
The tablet turned into energy as it dissolved
The water became lighter once the tablet reacted
b.why: The bubbles are a gas product that leaves the open cup, so its mass is no longer on the balance. The atoms were not destroyed. They are in the gas in the air.
b.clue: Where could the bubbles of gas have gone?

a.best: Atoms are rearranged, and none are made or lost

b.best: Gas escaped into the air, taking its mass with it
